newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end up slightly despite profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end up slightly despite profit-taking.

text.p: Thai stocks extended gains for the fourth day on Monday despite several bouts of profit-taking by local retail investors, brokers said.
The SET index finished 0.43 point higher to 948.52 on thin 2.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 0.05 point to 71.62.

"The market moved in a narrow range throughout the session today as investors watched for the release of third quarter financial results of finance firms. Some of them were better than earlier expectations," said Virat Tippanontakul of First Asia Securities.
National Finance and Securities was one of the major finance firms which did well, at least better than earlier expectations, in third quarter earnings, brokers said.
The firm said on Monday its net profit during the third quarter this year rose to 320.25 million baht versus 283.11 million baht, up 13.12 percent from the same period last year.
National Finance ended two higher at 55 baht.
Asia Credit also reported a quarterly rise to 258.1 million baht from 212.2 million baht a year ago. Its shares closed three baht higher at 125.
Brokers said the market was not active as investors watched for local political developments today, the first day for candidates to officially register for a November 17 general election.
National Finance and Securities topped the active list, rising two baht to 55. Siam Commercial Bank fell four to 200 while Finance One dipped two to 72.50 and Siam City Cement advanced 13 to 200.
Support is seen around 937 points on Tuesday and resistance at 963, brokers said.
